advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend the detector (or document the known gap) to catch variable-difference timing asserts like `end - t0 < N` where both operands are clock-derived, not only clock-call subtractions and timing-named identifiers.
evidence: scripts/check_wall_clock_asserts.py:76: `if isinstance(sub, ast.BinOp) and isinstance(sub.op, ast.Sub):` — only fires when a side is an `ast.Call` whose func name is in _CLOCK_CALLS

ABSENCE: no branch treats `end - t0` (two Name operands, neither a clock call, neither timing-named) as a wall-clock quantity, so `assert end - t0 < 1.0` is not detected
advisory.finding: The wall-clock detector misses upper-bound asserts formed from variable-to-variable time differences (e.g. `end = time.monotonic(); assert end - t0 < 1.0`): _has_timing_operand only matches names containing elapsed/duration/took or a subtraction whose operand is a clock CALL (time.monotonic()), not two plain time-valued variables. Such a site passes the gate despite being exactly the flake class the gate targets.
scenarios: A future test measures `start = time.monotonic(); ...; end = time.monotonic(); assert end - start < 2.0` — the gate stays green while the assert is a runner-contention flake.

advisory.finding: The lint's reversed-operand upper-bound branch (`N > elapsed` / `N >= elapsed`), an explicit code path in _upper_bound_wall_clock and a documented feature ('including reversed operands'), has no test that makes it FIRE. test_lower_bound_assert_is_silent only asserts silence for `elapsed > 0.2` (a genuine lower bound); a regression that dropped or broke the reversed branch would leave real flake-class asserts undetected and the suite green.
merged_from: The hang-guard marker-on-the-line-directly-above escape path (_marker_reason scans from start-2) is untested by the lint's own suite, even though it is the primary marker form used by every migrated real site in this diff. All marker tests place the comment inline on the assert; a regression breaking the above-line lookahead would silently re-flag (or, if inverted, silently exempt) real sites without failing the suite.

The `_ns` clock variants (monotonic_ns, perf_counter_ns) in _CLOCK_CALLS and clock-subtraction on the reversed operand are unexercised. Only bare `time.monotonic()` inline subtraction is tested (test_inline_monotonic_subtraction_fires), so a regression narrowing _CLOCK_CALLS or the subtraction-detection would not be caught for the *_ns forms.
